prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Landscape 16:9 original editorial cover for a Systems Safety Engineer in Robotics career guide. Visual thesis: understanding a robot means considering the whole system and the people around it. A dramatic close portrait of a gender-unspecified engineer wearing an invented futuristic graphite helmet with a broad smooth dark reflective visor, seen from a three-quarter side angle. The helmet and shoulder occupy the left two thirds of the composition; the face is completely hidden. In the curved visor reflection, a distant robot arm and a mobile machine can be recognized inside a dry, enclosed experimental test area with physical partitions. These are subtle realistic reflections, not holographic interfaces. The rest of the frame falls into a softly focused dark engineering environment. Photorealistic cinematic portrait with tactile visor reflections, matte graphite shell, fine fabric texture and controlled silver edge lighting. Approximately 85 percent black white gray and silver. Deliberate electric-lime accents occupy 10 to 15 percent, confined to a few physical helmet panels and thin lab status lights. Asymmetric intimate framing, quiet concentration, elegant and futuristic. No visible face or identifiable gender, no laptop, no legible screen, no printed safety labels, no text, words, numbers, diagrams, logos, watermark, paper texture, wet glass or rain. Do not depict this as actual protective equipment or a compliant installation; it is an invented conceptual editorial illustration, not a product photograph or safety instruction.
